claims.text: House-baked wheat sourdough bread is a centerpiece and lunch is sandwich-based, so flour is pervasive in the kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Vegetable dishes such as the Spanish tortilla contain eggs and pan con tomate is served with sheep's cheese and jamón, so vegetable plates are not reliably vegan.
Cooking centers on home-grown vegetables, so genuine vegetable-forward dishes (cauliflower potage, spinach tortilla) are available.

name: Pizzeria Icaro (ピッツェリア イーカロ)

claims.text: GF dough, pasta and desserts are made in an isolated dedicated gluten-free lab, separate from the wheat prep area, and GF pizza is served on a marked logo plate.
empacede reports GF pizzas are baked in a separate dedicated stone oven at a facility where wheat is not brought in, while regular wheat pizzas use the large in-store wood-fired oven.

This is nonetheless a full wheat pizzeria with an active wood-fired oven, so airborne flour and shared in-store handling remain a celiac cross-contact risk — confirm baking/plating separation on the day.
Shared kitchen with cheese, cured meats and seafood; vegan orders (e.g. Marinara) are not prepared in isolation.
The shop explicitly positions its gluten-free offering for people with celiac disease, gluten intolerance and allergies, and at least one blog notes egg-allergy accommodation.
Owner is a 2019 Naples gluten-free-category world champion pizzaiolo.
Dedicated GF lab, dedicated GF oven, GF crust for essentially the whole pizza menu, plus all-GF pasta and desserts, and a gluten-free beer (Orivia) on the drinks list.

name: 田舎料理 畔（ホトリ） (Inaka Ryori Hotori)

claims.text: Set lunches regularly feature deep-fried mains (fried horse mackerel, white fish fries, croquettes) made with wheat batter/breading, with no indication of a separate gluten-free preparation.
Dishes include soy-marinated and braised items (e.g., soy-soaked tuna, braised hamburger) and miso soup, which in standard Japanese home cooking use wheat-containing soy sauce and miso.
The kitchen's 'mago wa yasashii' approach intentionally includes fish, and mains include fish, tuna, pork, and beef, with side dishes and miso soup likely made with fish dashi.
Cooking is strongly vegetable- and produce-forward, using homegrown and seasonal Yamato-area vegetables and a balanced, health-minded menu philosophy.

name: 地酒BAR"なら" (Jizake BAR "Nara" (Sake BAR NARA))

claims.text: Snacks include cured, smoked, and pickled items typical of a sake bar, which commonly use soy-sauce-based seasonings (soy sauce normally contains wheat); no gluten-free claims are made.
Food program centers on house-made venison and wild boar, so plant snacks like smoked tofu and pickles are prepared in a meat-handling environment.
Sake is rice-based and naturally free of wheat and animal products, so the tasting flights are inherently safe for both wheat-avoidant and vegan drinkers.

No dedicated gluten-free kitchen or allergen handling is documented; while the noodles are 100% buckwheat with no wheat binder, sides such as persimmon-leaf sushi and inari and the soy-based broth share the same small kitchen.
The dipping broth (tsuyu) is a robust bonito-dashi Kansai-style sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned, so standard wheat-containing soy sauce should be assumed.
The standard soba broth is made with bonito (fish) dashi, so noodles served with broth are not vegan; a plant-based diner would need to confirm a fish-free option.
The noodles are jūwari — 100% buckwheat pounded with no wheat binder (つなぎなし) — which is unusual and means the noodle itself contains no wheat.

name: 懐石料理 円 (Kaiseki Ryori En (YEN))

claims.text: Signature dish is sake-lees tempura (wheat batter) and summer menus include somen (wheat noodles); cooking relies on soy-based seasonings and fish/kombu dashi. No gluten-free protocol is documented.
Standard kaiseki includes fish dishes (salted grilled mackerel) and dashi/egg; the kitchen is not vegan by default, so vegans must request plant-only preparation in advance.
The official site advertises guidance for vegetarian guests; reservations by phone with menu choice stated in advance are recommended, allowing accommodation to be discussed ahead.
Vegetable-centric seasonal cooking and explicit willingness to provide vegetarian guidance, with advance phone reservation, make plant-forward meals feasible.

name: 海鮮料理 つじ平 (Kaisen Ryori Tsujihira)

claims.text: Menu is heavy on tempura/fried fish, soy sauce and fish dashi; no gluten-free handling is documented, so cross-contact with wheat is expected.
Sashimi and grilled-fish dishes are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no tamari/GF soy sauce is mentioned.
Fish dashi and fish ingredients are central to nearly all dishes including soups and small plates; assume animal products throughout.

name: 柿の葉すし本舗たなか なら本店（柿の葉茶屋） (Kakinoha Sushi Honpo Tanaka Nara Honten (Kak)

claims.text: Eat-in sushi sets are accompanied by miso soup containing fu (wheat gluten), indicating wheat is present in the kitchen.
Sushi and accompanying sauces use standard Japanese soy sauce, which is brewed with wheat; no gluten-free soy alternative is indicated.
The menu is built around fish-topped sushi (mackerel, salmon, sea bream, conger eel, tuna), so shared surfaces and tools contact seafood; no separate vegan handling is documented.
